partners.diseaseBName: granulomatous disease, chronic, autosomal recessive, cytochrome b-positive, type 2
partners.mechanism_chain: CYBB (HGNC:2444) —DISRUPTS→ NADPH oxidase complex assembly and function (GO:0031140); NADPH oxidase complex assembly and function (GO:0031140) —DECREASES→ Reactive oxygen species (ROS) (CHEBI:17795); Reactive oxygen species (ROS) (CHEBI:17795) —LEADS_TO→ Susceptibility to mycobacterial infections (HP:0002726); NCF2 (HGNC:7728) —DISRUPTS→ NADPH oxidase complex assembly and function (GO:0031140); NADPH oxidase complex assembly and function (GO:0031140) —LEADS_TO→ Granulomatous disease (HP:0002727). Mutations in CYBB (Disease A) or NCF2 (Disease B) disrupt the assembly and function of the NADPH oxidase complex, leading to reduced production of reactive oxygen species (ROS). partners.mechanism_chain: CYBB (HGNC:2445) —DISRUPTS→ reactive oxygen species homeostasis (GO:0000302); reactive oxygen species homeostasis (GO:0000302) —LEADS_TO→ Increased susceptibility to mycobacterial infections (HP:0030117); P4HB (HGNC:8725) —DISRUPTS→ endoplasmic reticulum unfolded protein response (GO:0034996); endoplasmic reticulum unfolded protein response (GO:0034996) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal abnormalities (HP:0000924); endoplasmic reticulum unfolded protein response (GO:0034996) —LEADS_TO→ Microcephaly (HP:0000252). Loss of CYBB function impairs the ability to generate reactive oxygen species, crucial for combating mycobacteria, leading to susceptibility. Concurrently, loss of P4HB function disrupts the endoplasmic reticulum unfolded protein response, which is involved in protein folding and cellular stress management. Dysregulation of the UPR can indirectly impact ROS homeostasis and cellular defense mechanisms, potentially exacerbating susceptibility to infections and contributing to the skeletal and neurological phenotypes seen in Cole-Carpenter syndrome.

falsification.text: If studies demonstrate that mutations in CYBB do not affect ER stress markers or UPR activation, and conversely, if mutations in P4HB do not lead to alterations in ROS production or scavenging capacity in relevant cell types, this mechanistic link would be falsified.
falsification.gnomad_variant: While specific causal variants are not provided, if common variants (>1% allele frequency) in CYBB or P4HB in gnomAD are found to be associated with normal ROS homeostasis or UPR function respectively, it would weaken the proposed link.

partners.diseaseBName: methylmalonic aciduria and homocystinuria type cblC
partners.mechanism_chain: CYBB (HGNC:2406) —DISRUPTS→ NADPH oxidase complex activity (GO:0032081); NADPH oxidase complex activity (GO:0032081) —DECREASES→ Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) (CHEBI:17477); Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) (CHEBI:17477) —INCREASES→ Oxidative Stress Response (GO:0006974); Oxidative Stress Response (GO:0006974) —LEADS_TO→ Increased susceptibility to mycobacterial infections (HP:0002720); MMACHC (HGNC:24062) —DISRUPTS→ Methylmalonic Acid (CHEBI:16090); MMACHC (HGNC:24062) —DISRUPTS→ Homocysteine (CHEBI:17977); Methylmalonic Acid (CHEBI:16090) —LEADS_TO→ Methylmalonic aciduria (HP:0002170); Homocysteine (CHEBI:17977) —LEADS_TO→ Homocystinuria (HP:0000983); Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) (CHEBI:17477) —INCREASES→ Oxidative Stress Response (GO:0006974); Methylmalonic Acid (CHEBI:16090) —INCREASES→ Oxidative Stress Response (GO:0006974); Homocysteine (CHEBI:17977) —INCREASES→ Oxidative Stress Response (GO:0006974). CYBB deficiency impairs the NADPH oxidase complex, leading to reduced ROS production, which paradoxically compromises the immune response and increases susceptibility to mycobacterial infections. In contrast, MMACHC deficiency leads to the accumulation of methylmalonic acid and homocysteine. These accumulated metabolites can contribute to oxidative stress, which in turn can exacerbate cellular damage and contribute to the observed phenotypes. The convergence is on the shared pathway of oxidative stress response, where different upstream disruptions (impaired ROS production in disease A, and metabolite-induced ROS in disease B) lead to a dysregulated oxidative stress state.
